record.tranche_reason: The study compares apparent superposition in baseline and active-learning-trained ResNet-18 models using feature-clustering, cosine-similarity, and activation-maximization analyses, rather than reproducing the original neuron analysis.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes from several proxies for superposition. It does not report the classwise selection counts as a result about superposition, and the four randomly selected units are not identified as units responding to particular unrelated inputs.
record.test_reason: The study compares ordinary and least-confidence active-learning training of ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet, but its outcomes are not neuron-level polysemanticity measures. It reports class-cluster separation (t-SNE, silhouette, Davies-Bouldin) and cosine similarity of feature vectors, which are related but different constructs. Its only neuron-level evidence is activation maximization of four random units, which the author says is hard to interpret and not comparable across models. No row shows whether any neuron responds to unrelated inputs, or what share do, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author concludes that active learning performed worse and showed more superposition on both datasets, judged by proxies. The author suggests non-informative sample selection and overfitting to uncertain samples as causes. No accuracy figures are reported to back 'performs worse'.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet, comparing ordinary training with least-confidence active-learning sample selection. It does not reproduce the original neuron-level analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent outcome differs across datasets and proxies: on Tiny ImageNet the active-learning model has a lower mean cosine similarity, while clustering measures and the activation-maximization description point toward more overlap or superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Least-confidence active learning yields worse class-cluster separation than ordinary training on both datasets (t-SNE overlap, silhouette 0.189 vs 0.212 and -0.399 vs -0.348). Proxies disagree: CIFAR-10 Davies-Bouldin is slightly better under active learning, and Tiny ImageNet cosine similarity is lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-selection procedure (uncertainty-based active learning) changes representation-level proxies of superposition in CNN classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-maximization images of four random Layer4.1.conv2 units look noisier or more crowded under active learning. The author says they are hard to interpret and not comparable across models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data selection affects qualitative activation-maximization complexity of CNN units.

record.problems: The study uses indirect proxies for superposition rather than measuring the share of polysemantic neurons. Only four randomly selected units are visualized, their features are difficult to interpret, and units from separate models are not directly comparable. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the Tiny ImageNet Davies-Bouldin values are not given numerically.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome on the claim was left out.

untested.parts: No unit is shown responding to identified unrelated inputs.
Capacity and sparsity are not varied.
Activation function, architecture and regularization are not varied. No share of polysemantic neurons is measured, and accuracy is not reported numerically.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: A single-author, non-peer-reviewed preprint. Superposition is operationalized via class-clustering and cosine-similarity proxies, not neuron polysemanticity. It miscites Toy Models of Superposition as 'A mathematical framework' and cites Mu & Andreas for t-SNE. No uncertainty estimates are given and accuracy is not reported. The reader's V1 and V5 verdicts are removed: the rows do not measure the versions' constructs, and V5 concerns architecture or regularization, not data selection.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that any particular neuron responds strongly to multiple identified, unrelated inputs, or that this is common across image-classifier neurons.
No language models, transformer MLP neurons, or token/context responses are studied.
The study does not test whether superposition is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Initialization, regularization, training noise, and capacity sufficient for one neuron per feature are not tested.

The study varies data-selection/training procedure, not activation function, architecture, or regularization. It does not measure a share of polysemantic neurons or establish a performance cost quantitatively.
The study does not use improved explanations to determine whether apparently mixed units share one feature or job.
The study compares several superposition proxies, but does not vary activation range or explanation scoring for neuron-level explanations.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses polysemantic neurons (car/dog example) and superposition. The study then measures only proxies and does not test the claim.

tranche.reason: Outcomes are class-clustering (t-SNE, silhouette, Davies-Bouldin) and cosine-similarity proxies, not neuron-level polysemanticity measures. Activation-maximization shows four random units without naming unrelated preferred inputs. The varied factor is active-learning data selection, not the activation, architecture or regularization that V5 names. It measures a related but different construct, so it does not test any version.

source_check.notes: All 20 rows match the text. The study's superposition claims are the author's reading of proxy metrics from a single run with no seeds or error bars. The Tiny ImageNet cosine mean (0.254 vs 0.310) runs opposite to the other proxies, and the CIFAR-10 Davies-Bouldin index is slightly better for active learning (1.542 vs 1.551). The abstract says active learning did not outperform on accuracy, but the text gives no accuracy figures, so the record's capability=y flag has no reported numbers behind it.
